subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Autonomous Delivery Vehicles
description: A quick, practical guide to Autonomous Delivery Vehicles.

hook.text: Small, driverless pods are already delivering groceries and packages on sidewalks in some American and European cities.

buildup.text: Companies like Nuro and Starship built low-speed robots that navigate streets without a human on board.

discovery.text: These vehicles drive at walking speed, making them safer than full-size autonomous cars in residential areas.

twist.text: Delivery drones take automation airborne, with Amazon and Zipline flying packages to rural and suburban doorsteps.

climax.text: Whether on wheels or wings, autonomous delivery could remove millions of delivery van trips from congested roads.

punchline.text: The first self-driving vehicles you trust may carry your groceries, not you.

quiz.question: Why are sidewalk delivery robots considered safer than autonomous cars?
options: They operate at walking speed in low-risk areas

details.summary: Autonomous delivery vehicles are small self-driving robots and vans designed to transport packages and food without a human driver, operating on sidewalks or roads at low speeds.
details.whyItMatters: Last-mile delivery accounts for over half of total shipping costs. Autonomous vehicles promise to slash expenses, reduce traffic, and cut emissions from delivery fleets.
takeaways: Most operate at low speeds on sidewalks or bike lanes
Companies like Nuro and Starship lead the field
They aim to solve the expensive last-mile problem

faq.question: Are autonomous delivery robots legal on public sidewalks?
faq.answer: Laws vary by jurisdiction. Several US states and cities have passed rules allowing sidewalk delivery robots with weight and speed limits, while some European cities still restrict them.

faq.question: How do delivery bots handle theft or tampering?
faq.answer: They use locked compartments opened only by the recipient through an app, along with cameras and alarms that record interactions and deter interference.
